heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Belize
heroData.subtitle: Hire specific talent in Belize without a local entity
heroData.description: Utilize Employer of Record (EOR) services to hire compliant teams in Belize. Navigate the Labour Act Chapter 297 and Social Security mandates with ease.
heroData.bestFor: Companies testing the Belizean market or hiring remote support staff

steps.title: Requirement Analysis & Quote
steps.description: Define the employee's role, salary in BZD or USD, and benefits package. The EOR provider calculates the total cost of employment, including the employer's Social Security contributions (approx. 4-8%) and management fees. The quote often includes a detailed breakdown of statutory burden versus net take-home pay.

steps.title: Employment Contract Drafting
steps.description: The EOR drafts a locally compliant employment contract adhering to Belize's Labour Act Chapter 297. Key clauses include working hours (45 hours/week standard), overtime rates (1.5x), and termination notice periods. Contracts must be stamped by the Labour Department in some cases for work permits.

steps.title: Employee Registration
steps.description: The EOR registers the new hire with the Belize Social Security Board (SSB). Employee must provide a valid Social Security Card and identification. Income tax registrations are also processed if applicable. The TD-4 form is prepared for tax deductions.

steps.title: Onboarding & Payroll Setup
steps.description: Employee is added to the local payroll cycle. EOR sets up mechanisms for statutory deductions including Social Security and Income Tax (PAYE) if salary exceeds the tax-free threshold ($26,000 BZD/year). Direct deposit details are collected.

steps.title: Ongoing HR Support
steps.description: The EOR handles ongoing HR tasks such as leave management (vacation, sick, maternity), expense reimbursements, and annual tax form issuance (TD-4). They also manage termination procedures if required.

items.title: Permanent Establishment Risk
items.text: Using an EOR for extended periods (12-18+ months) or for revenue-generating roles can create a Permanent Establishment (PE) risk, potentially triggering corporate tax liabilities for the foreign parent company.

items.title: Probation Periods
items.text: Statutory probation periods in Belize are typically up to 6 months. During this period, termination is simpler but must still follow due process outlined in the Labour Act.

items.title: Notice Periods
items.text: Notice periods depend on tenure. For 6 months to 2 years of service, 2 weeks' notice is required. For 2+ years, 4 weeks' notice is standard. Payment in lieu of notice is permitted.

items.title: Misclassification
items.text: Avoid treating EOR employees as contractors. If they work set hours, use your equipment, and report to you, they must be employees to obtain full legal protections.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors through an EOR in Belize?
faqs.answer: Yes, EORs can manage contractor payments, often referred to as 'Agent of Record' services. However, strict misclassification rules apply.

faqs.question: Is 13th-month pay mandatory in Belize?
faqs.answer: No, a 13th-month salary is not legally mandated in Belize. However, performance-based bonuses or Christmas bonuses are common cultural benefits.

faqs.question: What currency are employees paid in?
faqs.answer: Employees are typically paid in Belize Dollars (BZD). The currency is pegged to the USD at 2:1 (2 BZD = 1 USD). Some EORs facilitate USD payments to foreign accounts if negotiated.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle work permits?
faqs.answer: Yes, EORs can sponsor work permits for foreign nationals. The process typically takes 4-8 weeks and requires proof that no local could fill the role.

faqs.question: Can I provide equity/stock options?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it can be complex. EORs often help structure 'shadow equity' or phantom stock plans to avoid direct shareholder complications for the foreign parent.

faqs.question: What happens if there is a labor dispute?
faqs.answer: The EOR, as the legal employer, handles the dispute. However, they will consult with you. Belize's Labour Department is pro-employee, so documentation is key.

faqs.question: Are intellectual property rights protected?
faqs.answer: Yes, standard EOR contracts include IP assignment clauses ensuring all work created by the employee belongs to the foreign client.

faqs.question: Can I convert an EOR employee to a direct hire later?
faqs.answer: Yes, most EORs allow conversion. A 'conversion fee' may apply depending on the contract terms and length of service.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum contract duration?
faqs.answer: Typically, EORs require a minimum 3-6 month commitment, but month-to-month options exist with higher management fees.

steps.title: Gross Pay Calculation
steps.description: Calculate gross salary including basic pay, overtime (1.5x regular rate), and allowances. Ensure compliance with the minimum wage of $5.00 BZD per hour (effective 2023).

steps.title: Social Security Deduction
steps.description: Apply the sliding scale for Social Security Deductions. Maximum insurable earnings are capped at $520 BZD/week. Weekly contributions are shared: Employee pays ~$23.40 maximum, Employer pays ~$28.60 maximum (for weekly wages >$500).

steps.title: Income Tax (PAYE) Withholding
steps.description: Deduct Income Tax for employees earning above the threshold ($26,000 BZD per year). Rate is flat 25% on chargeable income above the threshold. No other personal deductions apply.

steps.title: Net Pay Disbursement
steps.description: Disburse net salaries to employee bank accounts via direct deposit. Issue pay slips detailing gross pay, all deductions, and net pay. Electronic payslips are acceptable.

steps.title: Authorities Remittance
steps.description: Remit deducted taxes and social security contributions to the Belize Tax Service and Social Security Board, typically by the 14th of the following month to avoid penalties.

items.title: Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Failure to remit Social Security contributions by the deadline attracts a surcharge of 10% of the amount due, plus interest. It is strictly enforced.

items.title: Minimum Wage
items.text: The minimum wage was increased to $5.00 BZD ($2.50 USD) per hour across all sectors effective January 1, 2023. This is a flat rate for agriculture, shops, and domestic work.

items.title: Severance Pay
items.text: Employees with 5-10 years of service are entitled to 1 week's pay for each year of service upon termination. For 10+ years, it increases to 2 weeks' pay per year. Resignation after 10 years also triggers a gratuity.

items.title: Overtime Calculation
items.text: Overtime is calculated at 1.5x for ordinary days (beyond 9 hours) and 2.0x for work on Public Holidays or Sundays (if not a regular work day).

faqs.question: What is the tax-free personal allowance?
faqs.answer: The first $26,000 BZD (approx. $13,000 USD) of annual income is exempt from income tax for employed individuals.

faqs.question: Is overtime mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, work beyond 9 hours a day or 45 hours a week must be paid at 1.5 times the ordinary rate. Work on public holidays is paid at 2 times the ordinary rate.

faqs.question: Are electronic payslips legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, electronic payslips are legally accepted provided the employee has access to print or save them.

faqs.question: How do I calculate pro-rated pay?
faqs.answer: Pro-rated pay is typically calculated based on a 260-day work year or 22-day work month, depending on company policy.

faqs.question: How are bonuses taxed?
faqs.answer: Bonuses are treated as ordinary income and are subject to the standard 25% income tax if the employee's total annual income exceeds the $26,000 threshold.

faqs.question: Is there a mandatory private pension?
faqs.answer: No, there is no mandatory private pension pillar. The Social Security Board provides the only statutory pension. Many employers offer private provident funds as a benefit.

faqs.question: Can I pay in USD cash?
faqs.answer: While USD is widely accepted, payroll should be recorded in BZD. Paying loosely in cash (USD or BZD) without payslips is illegal and avoids statutory deductions.

items.title: Currency
items.text: Salaries are paid in BZD, pegged 2:1 to USD.

items.title: Frequency
items.text: Bi-monthly or monthly payments are standard.

items.title: Payslips
items.text: Electronic payslips are legally accepted.

items.title: Social Security Cap
items.text: Social Security contributions are capped at a weekly insurable earning of $520. Monthly calculations usually average 4.33 weeks. Max employee contribution is ~$23.40/week.

items.title: Income Tax Threshold
items.text: Annual income tax exemption is $26,000 BZD. Tax is 25% on income above this threshold.

items.title: Total Cost
items.text: Employer cost is generally Gross Salary + ~4-5% (SSB) + any optional benefits. There is no payroll tax for employers, only the SSB contribution.

items.title: Currency
items.text: All calculations are in Belize Dollars (BZD). 2 BZD = 1 USD.

steps.title: Determine Gross Pay
steps.description: Start with the agreed monthly gross salary in BZD.

steps.title: Check SS Band
steps.description: Consult the Social Security Benefit Schedule to find the exact weekly deduction. Cap is $23.40/week for employee.

steps.title: Calculate Taxable Income
steps.description: Subtract the $26,000 annual exemption (pro-rated monthly ~$2,166) from the monthly gross salary.

steps.title: Apply 25% Rate
steps.description: Apply 25% tax to the chargeable income (Gross - Exemption).

steps.title: Deduct
steps.description: Subtract Employee SS and Income Tax from Gross to get Net Pay.

faqs.question: Does this include health insurance?
faqs.answer: No, this calculation only covers statutory Social Security deductions. Private health insurance is separate.

faqs.question: Is the currency BZD or USD?
faqs.answer: Figures are in Belize Dollars (BZD). Convert to USD by dividing by 2.

faqs.question: Is there a payroll tax for employers?
faqs.answer: No, there is no separate payroll tax. Employers only pay their portion of Social Security.

items.title: Social Security
items.text: Capped at wages of $520 BZD/week.

items.title: Income Tax
items.text: Exemption on first $26,000 BZD of annual income.

items.title: Net Pay
items.text: Take-home pay is typically high due to the tax threshold.

heroData.title: Company Incorporation in Belize
heroData.subtitle: Formation of IBCs and LLCs
heroData.description: Establish a legal presence in Belize with an International Business Company (IBC) or Limited Liability Company (LLC). Quick setups and favorable tax regimes under the Business Companies Act.
heroData.bestFor: Asset protection, international trade, and tax planning

steps.title: Engage a Registered Agent
steps.description: Belize law requires international investors to work through a licensed local Registered Agent. You cannot directly approach the registry.

steps.title: Name Search & Reservation
steps.description: Submit proposed company names to the Belize Companies and Corporate Affairs Registry (BCCAR). Names must not be identical or deceptively similar to existing ones.

steps.title: Submission of Documents
steps.description: Submit Memorandum and Articles of Association (for IBC) or Articles of Organization (for LLC). Provide KYC documents for all directors/shareholders (passport copies, proof of address, bank reference).

steps.title: Payment of Government Fees
steps.description: Pay the registration fee. For standard capital (max $50,000 USD), the government fee is typically $100-$150 USD, plus agent fees. Total package often runs $800-$1500.

steps.title: Certificate of Incorporation
steps.description: Upon approval, the Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation. The entity is now legally formed. You will also receive an allotment of shares certificate and registers.

items.title: IBC vs LLC
items.text: IBCs (International Business Companies) are traditional offshore vehicles perfect for international trade. LLCs offer a structure similar to US LLCs, with pass-through taxation and asset protection features.

items.title: Economic Substance Act
items.text: Entities conducting 'relevant activities' (banking, insurance, shipping, HQ business) must demonstrate economic substance in Belize (office, employees, expenditure) to avoid penalties. Pure holding companies have reduced requirements.

items.title: Privacy
items.text: Belize offers high confidentiality. Detailed director/shareholder registers are kept by the Registered Agent but details are not publicly accessible on an open registry. Beneficial ownership information is filed with a secure government database.

items.title: No Audit Requirement
items.text: Standard IBCs and LLCs are generally not required to file audited financial statements unless they are regulated entities or meet certain revenue thresholds.

faqs.question: Do I need to visit Belize to open a company?
faqs.answer: No, the entire process can be done remotely through your Registered Agent. Courier services are used for physical documents if needed.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital requirement?
faqs.answer: There is no minimum paid-up capital requirement. Standard authorized capital is often $50,000 USD to keep government fees to the minimum tier.

faqs.question: Can I open a bank account with my Belize company?
faqs.answer: Yes, Belizean banks and international offshore banks accept Belize entities. However, due to rigorous compliance/KYC, opening a bank account can take 2-4 weeks or longer.
Yes, a single director and shareholder are permitted. They can be the same person. Corporate directors are also allowed.

faqs.question: What is the annual renewal date?
faqs.answer: Annual fees are typically due by July 31st each year. Late payments incur penalties and risk the company being struck off the register.

faqs.question: Are bearer shares allowed?
faqs.answer: No, Belize abolished bearer shares to comply with international anti-money laundering standards. All shares must be registered.

faqs.question: Can I re-domicile my company to Belize?
faqs.answer: Yes, companies incorporated in other jurisdictions can continue (re-domicile) into Belize provided they are in good standing.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for KYC?
faqs.answer: Standard KYC includes a certified passport copy (notarized), a recent utility bill (proof of address), and a professional reference letter (bank or lawyer).

faqs.question: How long does the name reservation last?
faqs.answer: A name reservation is typically valid for 30 days. It can be renewed if the incorporation process encounters delays.

faqs.question: Can I dissolve the company easily?
faqs.answer: Voluntary liquidation is a formal process involving a appointed liquidator. It takes 2-3 months. Simply stopping payments will lead to strike-off but may leave liabilities.

faqs.question: Is a company seal required?
faqs.answer: Yes, Belize companies typically adopt a company seal (common seal) for executing official deeds and documents, though digital signing is gaining acceptance.

items.title: Registered Agent
items.text: A licensed local Registered Agent is mandatory for international investors.

items.title: Privacy
items.text: Director registers are not publicly accessible.

items.title: Capital
items.text: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for IBCs.

heroData.title: Talent Acquisition in Belize
heroData.subtitle: Recruiting skilled English-speaking professionals
heroData.description: Access Belize's growing talent pool, particularly in BPO, customer service, and tourism sectors. English is the official language.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Leverage local job boards (Belize Jobs, LinkedIn) or specialized BPO recruitment agencies. Word-of-mouth and Facebook groups (e.g., 'Jobs in Belize') are also effective.

steps.title: Screening & Interviewing
steps.description: Conduct video or in-person interviews. Due to English being the primary language, language testing is rarely needed, but soft skills assessment is recommended for customer-facing roles.

steps.title: Background Checks
steps.description: Request police records (Police Record Certificate) for sensitive roles. Reference checks with past local employers are standard practice. Credit checks are less common.

steps.title: Offer & Negotiation
steps.description: Extend offer letters detailing salary (BZD), benefits, and working hours. Be clear if the salary is gross or net, as this is a common point of confusion.

steps.title: Pre-Employment Medical
steps.description: While not mandatory for all roles, some employers in tourism or labor-intensive industries require a basic medical check, which the employer often pays for.

items.title: Language Advantage
items.text: Belize is the only country in Central America with English as the official language, making it a prime location for voice-based BPO and customer support roles without the accent barrier often found in LatAm.

items.title: Salary Expectations
items.text: Customer service agents typically earn between $800 - $1,500 BZD per month ($400 - $750 USD). Senior roles or specialized tech talent command higher rates ($3000+ BZD).

items.title: Skill Scarcity
items.text: While strong in administrative and support roles, specialized senior technical talent (developers, data scientists) is scarce locally. Expats or remote training may be needed.

items.title: Education Level
items.text: The literacy rate is over 80%. The University of Belize produces graduates in business, IT, and tourism, providing a steady stream of entry-level talent.

faqs.question: Do I need a local entity to hire directly?
faqs.answer: Yes, to hire directly you need a local entity. Otherwise, you must use an EOR provider.

faqs.question: What is the standard work week?
faqs.answer: The standard work week is 45 hours. Most offices operate Monday to Friday 8am-5pm and Saturday mornings (often half-day).
Yes, but you must prove that no qualified Belizean is available. A Temporary Employment Permit is required, which takes time to process.

faqs.question: What about severance for short-term contracts?
faqs.answer: Fixed-term contracts end naturally without severance. However, repeated renewal of fixed contracts may be deemed continuous employment, triggering severance rights.

faqs.question: Are background checks legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, requiring a Police Record is standard. However, you must obtain the candidate's consent. Medical tests are also permitted for specific job functions.

items.title: Language
items.text: English is the official language, simplifying recruitment.

items.title: Work Permits
items.text: Foreign hires require proof that no local could fill the role.

items.title: Contracts
items.text: Written contracts are required by the Labour Act.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions in Belize
heroData.subtitle: Managing workforce data digitally
heroData.description: Adoption of Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS) in Belize is growing, particularly in BPO and larger enterprises moving away from spreadsheets.

items.title: Market Maturity
items.text: The Belizean market relies heavily on international HRIS platforms (like BambooHR, Zoho People) rather than distinct local software, due to the prevalence of English.

items.title: Integration
items.text: Look for systems that allow custom tax fields to handle Belize's specific Social Security bands (weekly caps differ per wage bracket) and Tax threshold calculations.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: Ensure cloud-based HRIS tools have offline capabilities or low-bandwidth modes if deploying in remote areas, though Belize City connectivity is generally stable.

items.title: Local Vendors
items.text: While scarce, some local IT firms offer custom-built payroll modules that integrate with QuickBooks, tailored specifically for Belizean tax laws.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Import employee data including Social Security Numbers and Tax IDs. Ensure historical leave balances are accurately transferred, especially for long-tenure staff due to severance rules.

steps.title: Policy Configuration
steps.description: Configure leave policies to match local law: 2 working weeks of annual leave, 16 days of sick leave per year (paid by SSB after first 3 days).

steps.title: Training
steps.description: Train local HR admins and managers. Self-service portals are increasingly popular for leave requests and payslip retrieval.

steps.title: Testing
steps.description: Run parallel payrolls (HRIS vs Legacy) for one month to verify deduction accuracy against the official SSB tables.

faqs.question: Are digital signatures on contracts valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, Belize recognizes electronic transactions and signatures under the Electronic Transactions Act.

faqs.question: Is data residency a concern?
faqs.answer: Belize does not have strict data localization laws requiring HR data to stay on-shore, so cloud hosts (AWS/Azure) in US regions are fully compliant.

faqs.question: Can HRIS handle SSB reporting?
faqs.answer: Global platforms typically don't auto-generate the specific Belize SSB reports. You may need to export data to CSV and format it manually.

items.title: Data Privacy
items.text: Data protection laws are evolving; secure cloud storage is recommended.

items.title: Internet
items.text: Ensure offline capabilities for remote areas.

items.title: SSB
items.text: Systems should handle Belize Social Security specific bands.

heroData.title: Accounting Services in Belize
heroData.subtitle: IFRS-compliant bookkeeping and reporting
heroData.description: Maintain financial health with local accounting standards. IFRS is the accepted standard for financial reporting in Belize.

steps.title: Record Keeping
steps.description: Maintain all invoices, receipts, and bank statements. Records must be kept in English and retained for a minimum of 6 years as per the Tax Administration Act.

steps.title: Monthly Reconciliation
steps.description: Reconcile bank accounts and ledgers. Prepare monthly Business Tax filings based on gross turnover. This differs from profit-based systems.

steps.title: GST Filing
steps.description: If registered for GST, file monthly returns netting output tax against input tax. Refunds can be claimed or carried forward.

steps.title: Annual Financial Statements
steps.description: Prepare annual financial statements in accordance with IFRS. These are required for the Annual Return to the registry and for banking compliance reviews.

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: Belize has adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as the national accounting standard for all companies.

items.title: Currency Denomination
items.text: While books can be kept in foreign currency (for IBCs), tax returns must often be converted to Belize Dollars at the official rate (2:1 USD).

items.title: Outsourcing
items.text: Many small to medium businesses outsource accounting to local firms to ensure compliance with the specific Business Tax turnover rules, which can be complex for specific industries.

items.title: Audit Thresholds
items.text: Private companies generally do not require a statutory audit unless gross receipts exceed a certain high threshold or for bank loan requirements.

faqs.question: Is an annual audit mandatory?
faqs.answer: Audits are generally not mandatory for small private companies unless specified by their articles or requested by shareholders. Regulated entities (banks, insurance) must be audited.

faqs.question: Can I use QuickBooks?
faqs.answer: Yes, QuickBooks and Xero are widely used in Belize. Many local accountants are certified in these platforms.

faqs.question: What happens if I lose my receipts?
faqs.answer: Tax authorities may disallow expenses if receipts are missing. In a Business Tax regime (turnover based), expenses are less critical for tax calculation but vital for internal profit tracking.

faqs.question: Can I change my fiscal year?
faqs.answer: Yes, companies can apply to the Tax Service to change their fiscal year-end, though the standard is the calendar year (Jan-Dec) or the government fiscal year (Apr-Mar).

faqs.question: Do I need a local accountant signature?
faqs.answer: For unaudited financial statements, a local accountant's signature is not strictly required by law, but banks often demand it for loan facilities or KYC reviews.

faqs.question: What are the penalties for errors?
faqs.answer: Penalties for incorrect returns can be up to 3 times the amount of tax exhausted. Voluntary disclosure usually mitigates this to a smaller fine and interest.

items.title: IFRS
items.text: Belize follows International Financial Reporting Standards.

items.title: Records
items.text: Keep financial records in legislation for at least 6 years.

items.title: Currency
items.text: Books can be in USD but reporting is often in BZD.

steps.title: License Renewal
steps.description: Renew Trade License annually. Fee depends on the annual rental value of the business premises.

steps.title: Annual Return Filing
steps.description: File Annual Return with the Companies Registry listing directors, shareholders, and capital structure. Due date varies by incorporation anniversary.

steps.title: Economic Substance Reporting
steps.description: Submit Economic Substance report annually if conducting relevant activities (e.g., HQ, shipping, IP business). Must demonstrate adequate spending and employees in Belize.

steps.title: BO Register Update
steps.description: Ensure the Register of Beneficial Owners is up to date with the Registered Agent. Any changes must be notified within 30 days.

items.title: Economic Substance Act (ESA)
items.text: Entities incorporated in Belize must show 'substantial economic presence' if they engage in relevant activities. Failure can lead to fines ($100k+) and strike-off.

items.title: Beneficial Ownership
items.text: A confidential Register of Beneficial Owners must be maintained at the Registered Office. This is not public but accessible by competent authorities.

items.title: Tax Compliance Certificate
items.text: Obtaining a Tax Compliance Certificate (TCC) is often required for government contracts or renewing certain licenses.
Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) like real estate agents and lawyers must register with the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) for AML compliance.

items.title: Record Retention
items.text: Companies must keep financial records, minutes of meetings, and registers for a minimum of 5 years at the registered office.

items.title: Substance Reporting Deadline
items.text: The Economic Substance Report is due within 9 months after the end of the fiscal year. Late filing incurs heavy daily penalties.

faqs.question: What is a 'Relevant Activity' for Economic Substance?
faqs.answer: Relevant activities include banking, insurance, fund management, financing & leasing, headquarters, shipping, holding company business, and IP business.

faqs.question: Can I use a virtual office?
faqs.answer: For basic presence, yes. However, to satisfy Economic Substance for relevant activities, a physical presence and local expenditure are often required.

faqs.question: How often is the Trade License paid?
faqs.answer: Trade License fees are assessed annually and are typically payable by December 31st for the upcoming year.

faqs.question: What are the penalties for late tax filing?
faqs.answer: Late filing of business tax returns incurs a penalty of 10% of the tax due or a minimum of BZD 10 per month, whichever is higher, plus interest.

faqs.question: Are surprise tax audits common?
faqs.answer: Surprise audits are rare but can occur if the Tax Service (BTS) detects significant discrepancies in turnover vs. expenses or VAT filings.

faqs.question: Can I appeal a tax fine?
faqs.answer: Yes, taxpayers have the right to appeal to the Income Tax Appeal Board within a specific timeframe (usually 15-30 days) after receiving the assessment.

items.title: Economic Substance
items.text: Relevant activities must show local presence.

items.title: Trade License
items.text: Must be renewed annually by December 31st.

items.title: UBO
items.text: Beneficial Owner registers are mandatory but private.

items.title: Business Tax (Turnover Tax)
items.text: Most companies pay Business Tax on gross turnover instead of Corporate Income Tax on profits. Rates vary: Trade (1.75%), Professional Services (6%), Financial Services (15%), Telecommunications (19%).

items.title: Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
items.text: Standard CIT of 25% generally applies to petroleum operations. Most other entities fall under the Business Tax regime.

items.title: General Sales Tax (GST)
items.text: GST is charged at 12.5% on most goods and services. Businesses with annual turnover >$75,000 BZD must register for GST.

items.title: Tax Holidays
items.text: The Fiscal Incentives Act allows for tax holidays of up to 5-10 years for approved development projects in tourism, agriculture, and manufacturing.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Register for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) with the Belize Tax Service (BTS). Register for GST if threshold is met (>75k BZD turnover).

steps.title: Monthly Declarations
steps.description: File monthly Business Tax returns on gross receipts by the 14th of the following month. GST returns are also due monthly on the same cycle.

steps.title: Payment
steps.description: Payments can be made online via the IRIS Belize portal or at local banks. Receipts must be retained as proof of tax standing.

steps.title: Annual Filing
steps.description: File annual returns reconciling monthly payments. Even if no business was conducted, 'Nil' returns must be filed to avoid penalties.

faqs.question: Is Belize a tax haven?
faqs.answer: Belize has modernized its tax laws to meet EU/OECD compliance (Economic Substance), moving away from a traditional 'tax haven' status, but still offers competitive low-tax structures for compliant businesses.

faqs.question: Are dividends taxable?
faqs.answer: Dividends paid by a company subject to Business Tax are generally exempt from further tax in the hands of the shareholder.
Withholding tax applies to payments to non-residents: 15% on management fees, technical services, and interest; 25% on other payments.

faqs.question: Is there a capital gains tax?
faqs.answer: Generally, there is no capital gains tax in Belize, except potentially on certain real estate transactions if deemed a trade.

faqs.question: What is the Hotel Tourist Tax?
faqs.answer: Accommodations must collect a 9% Hotel Tourist Tax from guests, which is remitted to the Belize Tourism Board, distinct from GST.

faqs.question: Do I need to file if I have no income?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Nil' returns must be filed monthly for Business Tax and GST to confirm no activity and avoid non-filing penalties.

items.title: Business Tax
items.text: Tax is often based on turnover, not just profit.

items.title: Sales Tax
items.text: GST is 12.5% for applicable goods and services.

items.title: Fiscal Year
items.text: Standard fiscal year matches the calendar year.

heroData.title: M&A and Legal Services in Belize
heroData.subtitle: Transactions and contracts
heroData.description: Legal frameworks for Mergers & Acquisitions, contract law, and corporate restructuring in Belize. British Common Law foundation.

steps.title: Due Diligence
steps.description: Conduct financial and legal due diligence. Verify good standing, tax compliance, pending litigation, and title to any real estate assets.

steps.title: Deal Structuring
steps.description: Structure the deal as a share purchase or asset purchase. Share transfers attract Stamp Duty (typically 2-5%), while asset transfers may attract GST.

steps.title: Regulatory Approval
steps.description: For regulated industries (banking, telecom), Central Bank or PUC approval may be required prior to change of control.

steps.title: Drafting Agreements
steps.description: Draft Share Purchase Agreement (SPA) or Asset Purchase Agreement (APA). Include warranty clauses and indemnities particular to local risks.

steps.title: Closing & Transfer
steps.description: Execute Share Transfer Instruments. Update the Register of Members and file changes with the Companies Registry. Pay applicable Stamp Duties.

items.title: Common Law
items.text: Belize's legal system is based on English Common Law, making it familiar to investors from the US, UK, and Canada. The Privy Council in London remains the final court of appeal.

items.title: Land Ownership
items.text: Foreigners have the same rights as locals to buy and own land in Belize. However, 'Alien Landholding License' requirements were abolished, simplifying the process.

items.title: Stamp Duty
items.text: Transfer of land incurs Stamp Duty, usually 5% for residents and 8% for non-residents (after the first $20,000 exemption).

items.title: Contract Enforcement
items.text: Contracts are legally binding and enforceable. However, court processes can be slow, so arbitration clauses are recommended.

faqs.question: Can I enforce foreign judgments?
faqs.answer: Yes, foreign judgments can be enforced in Belize, particularly from Commonwealth jurisdictions, through registration in the Supreme Court.

faqs.question: Is arbitration available?
faqs.answer: Yes, Belize is a signatory to the New York Convention on arbitration. Arbitration clauses in contracts are upheld.

faqs.question: Are electronic contracts valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Electronic Transactions Act, electronic contracts and signatures have full legal effect.

faqs.question: How long does a merger take?
faqs.answer: A straightforward private share acquisition can close in 2-4 weeks. Asset deals or those requiring regulatory approval (banking/telecom) can take 3-6 months.

faqs.question: Are there antitrust regulations?
faqs.answer: Belize does not have a comprehensive competition law regime like the US/EU, but specific sectors (utilities) have regulations preventing monopolies.

faqs.question: Can I acquire a government listed asset?
faqs.answer: Privatization of government assets is rare and subject to specific parliamentary acts and public tender processes.

heroData.title: Software & Tech in Belize
heroData.subtitle: Emerging tech ecosystem
heroData.description: While still developing, Belize's tech scene offers opportunities for digital services and connectivity. Growing community of remote workers.

items.title: Internet Connectivity
items.text: Fiber optic internet is available in major towns (Belize City, San Pedro, San Ignacio) via providers like Digi (BTL) and Smart. Speeds up to 500Mbps are available.

items.title: Reliability
items.text: Power outages can occur, though they are less frequent in tourist hubs. Backup power (UPS/Generator) is recommended for critical operations.

items.title: Local Vendors
items.text: For hardware and basic IT support, local vendors exist in Belize City. For complex custom software development, hiring remote or nearshore talent is common.

items.title: Tech Hubs
items.text: San Pedro (Ambergris Caye) and Placencia are popular with digital nomads due to lifestyle and connectivity, although Belize City remains the business center.

steps.title: Identify Needs
steps.description: Determine if you need on-site hardware support (requires local vendor) or software development (cloud-based/remote).

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Key local providers include Fultec Systems and Business Computer Systems for hardware. For software custom dev, check firms like Idea Lab Studios or freelancers on Upwork.

steps.title: Contracting
steps.description: Service Level Agreements (SLAs) are crucial given the variance in infrastructure stability. Negotiate response times for outages.

steps.title: Remote Setup
steps.description: If setting up a remote team, procure MiFi devices or Starlink (now licensed) as backup internet solutions.

faqs.question: Is Starlink available?
faqs.answer: Starlink has been granted a license to operate in Belize as of 2024/2025, improving connectivity options for remote areas significantly.

faqs.question: Are there tech parks?
faqs.answer: There are no dedicated 'tech parks' yet, but Belize City serves as the commercial and connectivity hub.
4G LTE is available in all major towns and highways. Remote areas may have spotty coverage.

faqs.question: What is the cost of software developers?
faqs.answer: Local junior developers earn $1,500-$2,500 BZD/month. Seniors are rare but can command $4,000+ BZD/month or work for foreign clients directly.

faqs.question: Are there co-working spaces?
faqs.answer: Yes, co-working spaces are emerging in Belize City (e.g., The Ubiquitous) and San Pedro, catering to digital nomads.

faqs.question: What tech stacks are common?
faqs.answer: The local market is heavily influenced by US trends. PHP/Laravel, .NET, and increasingly React/Node.js are common. WordPress is dominant for web agencies.

faqs.question: Is crypto legal for payments?
faqs.answer: Crypto is not legal tender, but there is no explicit ban on private transactions. However, tax implications are grey, and businesses usually convert to fiat for compliance.

faqs.question: Are there tech meetups?
faqs.answer: Tech meetups are infrequent but growing. The Belize Chamber of Commerce occasionally hosts digital transformation events.

items.title: Power
items.text: UPS backups are recommended due to occasional outages.

items.title: Talent
items.text: San Pedro is a growing hub for digital nomads.

heroData.title: Marketing in Belize
heroData.subtitle: Reaching the Caribbean and Central American audience
heroData.description: Leverage local digital agencies to navigate the multicultural and multilingual Belizean market. Focus on tourism and local retail.

items.title: Social Dominance
items.text: Facebook is the absolute dominant platform for business in Belize. WhatsApp is the primary tool for customer communication and support.

items.title: Tourism Focus
items.text: Much of the high-end marketing expertise is centered around tourism (resorts, tours). Agencies in this niche are high quality and understand international appeal.

items.title: Traditional Media
items.text: Radio is still very influential in Belize for reaching local populations outside the digital bubble. Newspaper ads are used for formal notices.

items.title: Influencers
items.text: Local micro-influencers are gaining traction, especially in the food and lifestyle segments. They are cost-effective for brand awareness.

steps.title: Agency Selection
steps.description: Choose agencies with specific experience in your sector. Notable names include McNab Design, Idea Lab Studios, and BK Creative.

steps.title: Localization
steps.description: Ensure content resonates in both English (official) and Spanish/Kriol where appropriate for broader reach. Visuals should reflect Belize's diversity.

steps.title: Channel Strategy
steps.description: Allocate budget heavily towards Facebook Ads and potentially local radio spots for mass market awareness. Instagram is key for younger demographics.

steps.title: Print Media
steps.description: For B2B or formal announcements, consider ads in the Amandala or Reporter newspapers.

faqs.question: What is the best time for campaigns?
faqs.answer: Tourism campaigns peak before the high season (November). Retail peaks around Christmas, Easter, and September Celebrations.

faqs.question: Is influencer marketing effective?
faqs.answer: Yes, micro-influencers and local personalities are effective, particularly within the lifestyle and food sectors.
English is sufficient for 90% of campaigns, but Spanish adds reach heavily in Northern and Western districts.

faqs.question: What is the main TV provider?
faqs.answer: Cable TV is popular (Digi, various local operators). Advertising on local news channels (Channel 5, Channel 7) is high-impact.

faqs.question: How do I pay for Facebook Ads?
faqs.answer: You typically need a credit card. Note that Belizean banks may charge a foreign transaction fee for USD payments to Meta/Google.

items.title: Social Media
items.text: Facebook is the primary business directory and ad platform.

items.title: Language
items.text: Ads in English work best, with Spanish for specific regions.

items.title: Tourism
items.text: Peak ad season aligns with tourism high season (Nov-Apr).
